data.title: Russian strikes kill 11 including 3 children, says Kyiv
data.description: KYIV - Russian strikes on the southeastern city of Zaporizhzhia on Saturday killed at least 11 people, including three children, according to regional authorities in Ukraine.

data.title: Indian ‘cockroach’ leaders detained ahead of major protest
data.description: NEW DELHI - Indian police detained the head of the satirical Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) online movement on Saturday ahead of a major protest it called against the Election Commission, the party said.

data.title: Gaza ceasefire promises mostly unfulfilled
data.description: JERUSALEM - One year after US President Donald Trump declared the war in Gaza to be over, few of the long-term promises of the ceasefire have come to fruition.

data.title: Trump hails deal with Russia to release diesel
data.description: WASHINGTON - US President Donald Trump said on Friday that he had secured Russia’s agreement for a major release of diesel, as he eased war sanctions on Moscow in a push to lower energy costs ahead of midterm elections.

data.title: Taiwan increasing defence spending to ‘deter war’
data.description: TAIPEI - Taiwan aims to “deter war” by increasing its defence spending, the democratic island’s leader said on Saturday, as China uses military pressure to assert its territorial claims.

data.title: Three Mexicans convicted of murdering Australian, US surfers
data.description: ENSENADA (MEXICO) - A Mexican judge on Friday convicted three men ENSENADA, Mexico - A Mexican judge on Friday convicted three men in the 2024 murders of two Australian surfers and their American friend, who were killed during a botched robbery that sparked international outrage.

data.title: Major earthquake rocks Panama, triggers tsunami warning
data.description: SANTIAGO DE VERAGUAS (PANAMA) - A magnitude-7.7 earthquake rocked Panama on Friday, unleashing panic in the high-rise capital city and causing buildings to collapse in the center of the country.

data.title: Flydubai co-pilot planned suicide attack on Tel Aviv airport: UAE prosecutor
data.description: DUBAI - The co-pilot who attacked the captain of a flydubai jet last month had planned to crash the plane into Tel Aviv's international airport, the United Arab Emirates' top prosecutor said on Friday.

data.title: Indian jailed in France for leading sadist Nazi cult that tortured girls
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - A Paris court on Friday jailed a young Indian man to 20 years jail for leading a masculinist group that forced young girls, many of them minors, to perform sexual acts and in some cases tortured them.

data.title: Hurricane Isaias approaches US Gulf Coast
data.description: PENSACOLA, Florida - Hurricane Isaias strengthened into a major category 3 storm Friday as it barrels towards the US Gulf Coast, the National Hurricane Center said, with landfall expected in Florida, Alabama or Mississippi in the next 24 hours.

data.title: Talks with Iran can only succeed without threats, says president
data.description: ASHGABAT, Turkmenistan - Peace negotiations with Iran would only succeed without “pressure and threats”, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said Friday, amid deadlocked efforts to end months of fighting in the Middle East.

data.title: EU: Turkey’s human rights record a bar to membership
data.description: TURKEY - The European Union said on Friday it had “serious concerns” about democratic standards in Turkey, warning that a crackdown on rights was further undermining Ankara’s long-stalled bid to join the bloc.

data.title: Two Renoir paintings stolen in France recovered
data.description: NICE, France - Two paintings by French master Pierre-Auguste Renoir have been recovered a month after they were stolen from a museum in southern France, the town’s mayor said Friday.

data.title: South African judge Navi Pillay wins Nobel Peace Prize
data.description: The Nobel Peace Prize was awarded on Friday to Navi Pillay, the South African judge who headed the Rwanda genocide tribunal and who last year presided over a UN commission that accused Israel of genocide in Gaza.

data.title: Eritrea and Ethiopia trade barbs as Tigray rebels retreat
data.description: ADDIS ABABA - Ethiopia and Eritrea each accused the other of starting a war of aggression on Friday as an internal Ethiopian conflict threatened to escalate into a regional war.

data.title: Saudi Arabia says three killed at airport as Yemen war expands
data.description: RIYADH — Saudi Arabia said on Friday that three people were killed including a pilot were killed in attacks on Riyadh's international airport, after Yemen's Houthis claimed a series of attacks targeting the facility.

data.title: Orangutans being rescued from Indonesia fires
data.description: PALANGKARAYA (INDONESIA) - An orangutan clings to the top of a mostly leafless tree in Indonesia's Borneo, as waves of thick smoke from the forest fires burning below waft over her.

data.title: Ukraine takes Russia fight to 'scorching sands' of Sahel
data.description: ABIDJAN - Ukraine has vowed to counter Russia wherever it can, even "in the scorching sands" of the Sahelian desert, as evidence mounts that Kyiv is backing Tuareg separatists battling Mali's army and its Russian allies.

data.title: Vietnam to host 76th Miss Universe competition in 2027
data.description: The Miss Universe Organization has announced that Vietnam will host the 76th Miss Universe competition in 2027, with the host city, venue and dates to be confirmed.

data.title: US to livestream Fort Hood shooter's execution by firing squad
data.description: Death sentence will be at Fort Hood on Dec 3, Hegseth says, as execution would ​be first by US military firing squad since 1945

data.title: US activists deploy poll volunteers over Trump intimidation fears
data.description: WASHINGTON — United States civil rights and pro-democracy groups have begun sending out trained volunteers to counter the possible deployment of armed federal agents to polling locations ahead of next month's midterm elections.

data.title: Okinawa resolution calls for revision of US forces pact after murder
data.description: TOKYO - Okinawan lawmakers adopted a resolution on Friday calling for revisions to a pact seen as giving the United States military preferential treatment in Japan, following a murder allegedly committed by an American Marine.

data.title: New York mayor says asking Trump to withdraw ICE after shooting
data.description: NEW YORK - New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani said on Thursday he would ask US President Donald Trump to remove federal immigration agents from the city as tensions flared over the latest shooting involving ICE.

data.title: Verdict over murders of Australia, US surfers expected on Friday in Mexico trial
data.description: ENSENADA (MEXICO) - A Mexican judge is expected to hand down his verdict on Friday in the high-profile murder trial of three men accused of killing two Australian surfers and their American friend in 2024.
